We develop UNICASE for the Eclipse platform with the Eclipse Java IDE.

We currently use the following development tools:

    * [http://java.sun.com/javase/downloads/index_jdk5.jsp Java 5 SE]
    * [http://phoenix.eclipse.org/packages/ Eclipse 3.5: Modeling Tools Edition] (Galileo)
          o EMF <br>
          o GEF, GMF <br>
          o Ecore Tools <br>

    * Eclipse Plugins (install via Update Manager)
          o Subclipse: http://subclipse.tigris.org/update_1.6.x<br>
            o If you are not using Windows 32 Bit you might run into problems with Subclipse because Java is started in 64bit mode by default. Here is a possible solution for the problem http://subclipse.tigris.org/wiki/JavaHL <br>
          o UNICASE: http://unicase.googlecode.com/svn/updatesite/internal/ <br>
          o COPE: http://cope.in.tum.de/update-site/site.xml<br>
            o NOTE: If you have already installed the runtime feature from the UNICASE update site, you will be notified.<br>
          o Checkstyle (use version 4.4.x - check the *version* number): - http://eclipse-cs.sourceforge.net/update<br>
          o Findbugs (for static code checking): http://findbugs.cs.umd.edu/eclipse<br>
          o SWTBOT (for UI testing): Please find [http://www.eclipse.org/swtbot/downloads.php here] the update site that is compatible with your eclipse version<br>


Getting started as developer in 7 easy steps:

1. Download and install [http://java.sun.com/javase/downloads/index_jdk5.jsp Java].

2. Download [http://phoenix.eclipse.org/packages/ Eclipse] and install the required plugins (see above).

3. Checkout the UNICASE source code from the [http://code.google.com/p/unicase/wiki/SVN_Repository svn repository] (see this link: http://code.google.com/p/unicase/source/checkout) into your Eclipse workspace using Subclipse. Please see also this [CheckoutTutorial Tutorial]

4. Configure Java and Checkstyle warnings as described in [http://code.google.com/p/unicase/wiki/Coding_Guidelines Coding Guidelines].

5. Start the UNICASE server from Eclipse, see this [http://code.google.com/p/unicase/wiki/RunServerTutorial video tutorial].

6. Start the UNICASE client from Eclipse, see this [http://code.google.com/p/unicase/wiki/RunClientTutorial video tutorial].

7. Register for our [http://code.google.com/p/unicase/wiki/Mailinglist mailinglists].


If you have any questions please consider the FAQ and Developer FAQ and do not hesitate to use our mailinglist.

Note: We use UNICASE to model UNICASE, also called boot strapping or eat-your-own-dogfood.See [http://code.google.com/p/unicase/wiki/Unicase_repository_beta_server here] for details.
